questions.question: Veer Surendra Sai was a freedom fighter from:
questions.solution:
The correct answer is Odisha.
Veer Surendra Sai was a freedom fighter from Odisha. He started his revolt against British rule long before 1857 and continued his guerrilla war against British authority from 1857 till 1864.

questions.question: Who was the first general secretary of the All India Farmer's Congress?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is N.G. Ranga.
N.G. Ranga was the first general secretary of the All India Farmer's Congress. He was a freedom fighter from Andhra Pradesh and received the Padma Vibhushan for his contributions to the peasants' movement.

questions.question: Who among the following was a leader who led a revolt against British rule from North East India?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is Rani Gaidinliu.
Rani Gaidinliu was a Naga spiritual and political leader who led a revolt against British rule in North East India. At the age of 13, she joined the Heraka religious movement established by her cousin Haipou Jadonang in Manipur.

questions.question:
Consider the following statements:
Statement 1: Bal Gangadhar Tilak's Home Rule Movement was mainly active in Maharashtra.
Statement 2: Annie Besant's Home Rule Movement was mainly active in Punjab.
Which one of the above statements is correct?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is Statement 1 only.
  • Statement 1 is correct: Bal Gangadhar Tilak's Home Rule Movement (launched in 1916) was primarily centered in Maharashtra. He published his ideas through 'Kesari' (Marathi) and 'Mahratta' (English).
  • Statement 2 is incorrect: Annie Besant's Home Rule Movement was mainly active in Madras (Chennai), not Punjab.

questions.question: Which of the following organisations, divided into two branches, was established by Lokmanya Bal Gangadhar Tilak and Annie Besant?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is Home Rule League.
In April 1916, Tilak founded the Indian Home Rule League with headquarters in Poona. In September 1916, Annie Besant founded the All-India Home Rule League based in Madras. Thus, the movement had two branches.

questions.question:
Assertion (A): Mahatma Gandhi suspended the Non-Cooperation Movement in February 1922.
Reason (R): The Chauri Chaura incident in the United Provinces turned the movement violent when protesters set a police station on fire, killing policemen.
questions.option_1: Both A and R are true, and R is the correct explanation of A
questions.option_2: Both A and R are true, but R is not the correct explanation of A
questions.option_3: A is true, but R is false
questions.option_4: A is false, but R is true
questions.solution:
The correct answer is Both A and R are true, and R is the correct explanation of A.
The Chauri Chaura incident took place in Gorakhpur district of United Provinces (now Uttar Pradesh). Protesters set a police station on fire, killing 22 policemen. Mahatma Gandhi halted the Non-Cooperation Movement on 12th February 1922 because the movement turned violent, which was against his principle of non-violence.

questions.question: Indian National Army was formed in which of the following countries?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is Singapore.
The Indian National Army (INA), also known as the Azad Hind Fauj, was a collaborationist armed unit of Indian supporters that fought under the command of the Japanese Empire. It was founded by Mohan Singh in September 1942 in Singapore during World War II.

questions.question: Being the President of the Indian National Congress, who among the following had called for complete independence from the British Raj in 1929?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is Jawaharlal Nehru.
In December 1929, Jawaharlal Nehru was chosen as the President of the Indian National Congress during its annual session in Lahore. At this event, he raised the tricolour flag on the banks of the Ravi River and called for complete independence (Purna Swaraj) from British rule.

questions.question: On 31 October 1940, who among the following was arrested for offering individual Satyagraha to protest against India's forced participation in the Second World War?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is Jawaharlal Nehru.
On 31 October 1940, Jawaharlal Nehru was arrested for participating in individual Satyagraha, protesting against India's forced involvement in the Second World War. During this period, Nehru spent approximately nine years in jail between 1921 and 1945.

questions.question:
Consider the following statements regarding the Indian National Army (INA):
1. It was founded by Mohan Singh in September 1942 in Southeast Asia during World War II.
2. Subhas Chandra Bose later became the supreme leader of the INA.
3. Rabindranath Tagore was one of the commanders of the INA.
Which of the statements given above is/are correct?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is 1 and 2 only.
  • Statement 1 is correct: INA was founded by Mohan Singh in September 1942 in Southeast Asia.
  • Statement 2 is correct: Subhas Chandra Bose later became the supreme leader of the INA.
  • Statement 3 is incorrect: Rabindranath Tagore was a poet and writer, not a commander of the INA.

questions.question: What is the name of the famous British social reformer known for founding the Indian Home Rule League in 1916?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is Annie Besant.
Annie Besant, an Irish theosophist, started the Home Rule movement in India in 1916, demanding self-government similar to the Irish Home Rule League. She founded the Home Rule League in Madras in September 1916 and established over 200 branches across India.

questions.question:
Consider the following statements:
Statement 1: Rabindranath Tagore renounced his knighthood in protest against the Jallianwala Bagh massacre.
Statement 2: The Simon Commission was set up in 1919 to investigate the incident.
Which of the above statements is/are true?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is 1 only.
  • Statement 1 is correct: Rabindranath Tagore renounced his knighthood in protest against the Jallianwala Bagh massacre (13th April 1919).
  • Statement 2 is incorrect: The Hunter Commission (not Simon Commission) was set up in 1919 to investigate the Jallianwala Bagh massacre. The Simon Commission came to India in 1928.

questions.question: Who among the following was one of the founders of the Swaraj Party?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is Chittaranjan Das.
The Swaraj Party, initially called the Congress Khilafat Swaraj Party, was established in 1923 by Chittaranjan Das and Motilal Nehru. This formation took place after the Gaya Annual Conference of the Indian National Congress in December 1922.

questions.question: Which of the following Satyagrahas was started by Dr B R Ambedkar in 1927?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is Mahad Satyagraha.
Mahad Satyagraha (also known as the Chavdar Tank Satyagraha) was started by Dr. B.R. Ambedkar in 1927 in Mahad (Raigad), Maharashtra. It centered around the Chavdar Tank, a public water source that was reserved exclusively for upper castes.

questions.question: Who among the following leaders founded the women's wing of Congress in 1940?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is Sucheta Kriplani.
Sucheta Kriplani founded the women's wing of Congress in 1940. She was the first female Chief Minister of Uttar Pradesh (1963-67). She sang Vande Mataram on 14th August 1947 in the opening session of Parliament.

questions.question: On 15 August 1947, the first prime minister of India, Jawaharlal Nehru, raised the Indian National Flag above the ______ of Red Fort in Delhi.
questions.solution:
The correct answer is Lahori Gate.
On 15 August 1947, Jawaharlal Nehru raised the Indian National Flag above the Lahori Gate of the Red Fort in Delhi. The National Flag of India was adopted on 22 July 1947, designed by Pingali Venkayya.

questions.question: Who moved the resolution proposing that the National Flag of India be a 'horizontal tricolor of saffron, white and dark green in equal proportion'?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is Jawaharlal Nehru.
Jawaharlal Nehru moved the resolution proposing the National Flag of India as a horizontal tricolor of saffron, white and dark green in equal proportion. The Tricolour was adopted as our national flag at a Congress Committee meeting in Karachi in 1931.

questions.question: Who among the following was the founder of 'Tiger Legion' or 'Free India Legion'?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is Subhas Chandra Bose.
Subhas Chandra Bose founded Azad Hind Fauj. The 'Tiger Legion' (Free India Legion) was formed in 1941 with the help of the German Government to fight against the British.

questions.question:
Consider the following statements regarding the Komagata Maru incident:
1. The Komagata Maru, carrying Indian passengers, was denied permission to land in Canada in 1914.
2. The ship was denied entry at Sydney harbour in Australia.
Which of the above statements is/are correct?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is 1 only.
The Komagata Maru was a coal-transport steamship converted into a passenger ship by Hong Kong-based businessman Gurdit Singh. It set off from Hong Kong in April 1914, reaching Vancouver's harbour in Canada (not Sydney, Australia) with 376 people on board, most of them Sikhs. It was denied permission to land in Canada in 1914. The ship ended up back in India on 29th Sep 1914 at Budge Budge, Calcutta.

questions.question: The origin of Directive Principles of State Policy can be traced to which of the following?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is Karachi Resolution (1931).
The origin of the Directive Principles of State Policy can be traced to the Karachi Resolution of 1931. The Karachi Session of Congress in 1931 was presided over by Sardar Vallabhbhai Patel. The Gandhi-Irwin Pact was signed on 5 March 1931, marking the end of civil disobedience.

questions.question: Who among the following freedom fighters was one of the founders of the Ferguson College in Pune in 1885?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is Bal Gangadhar Tilak.
Bal Gangadhar Tilak was one of the founders of Ferguson College in Pune in 1885. Other co-founding members included Vaman Shriram Apte, Vishnushashtri Chiplunkar, Mahadeo Ballal Namjoshi, and Gopal Krishna Agarkar.

questions.question: Motilal Nehru, C.R. Das gave up their legal practices during which Movement?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is Non-Cooperation Movement (1920-1922).
The Non-Cooperation Movement was organized by Mahatma Gandhi to obtain self-governance. Many lawyers gave up their practices during this movement, including Motilal Nehru, C.R. Das (Chittaranjan Das), C. Rajagopalachari, Saifuddin Kitchlew, Vallabhbhai Patel, Asaf Ali, T. Prakasam, and Rajendra Prasad.

questions.question: When was Alluri Sitarama Raju arrested ending a two-year armed tribal struggle?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is May 1924.
Alluri Sitarama Raju was publicly executed in Koyyuru on May 7, 1924 after being tied to a tree and shot. In August 1922, he launched the Rampa Rebellion (Namyam Rebellion) against the British. During this rebellion, he was helped by Bobbili Dora.

questions.question: Who among the following translated the play 'Neel Darpan' into English?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is Michael Madhusudan Dutt.
'Neel Darpan' is a Bengali-language play written in 1858-59 by Dinabandhu Mitra, depicting the oppression of indigo farmers. It was translated into English by Michael Madhusudan Dutt.

questions.question:
Consider the following pairs of historical events and the individuals associated with them:
1. Indigo Revolt - Digambar Biswas
2. Munda Rebellion - Birsa Munda
3. Santhal Rebellion - Sido and Kanhu
4. Paika Rebellion - Bakshi Jagabandhu
How many of the above pairs are correctly matched?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is All four.
  • Indigo Revolt (1859-60) was led by Digambar Biswas and Bishnu Biswas - Correct
  • Munda Rebellion (1899-1900) was led by Birsa Munda - Correct
  • Santhal Rebellion (1855-56) was led by Sido and Kanhu - Correct
  • Paika Rebellion (1817) was led by Bakshi Jagabandhu in Odisha - Correct
